scope: Cross-surface authz boundaries, phone-only lookup risk, mobile↔POS handoff trust, audit-log gap on cross-surface ops

findings.title: Phone-only customer lookup enables impersonation
findings.finding: LoyaltyController::check (line 71-77) accepts either loyalty_code OR phone number. /loyalty/scan (line 619-627) accepts either loyalty_code OR phone after preg_replace normalization. Phone is the LEAST secret credential — printed on receipts, often shared, available in contact lists. Anyone who knows a customer's phone number can call /api/loyalty/check (auth:sanctum required since SEC-CRIT FIX, throttle:10,1) and learn that customer's loyalty_code + name + balance + discount value. After scraping loyalty_code, attacker can redeem at any kiosk (no second factor — see PLOY-2-R-04).
findings.impact: Identity theft + financial loss. Particularly bad combined with PLOY-2-R-07 (cashier collusion) — cashier already knows customer phones from POS history.
findings.remediation: Either (a) remove phone-as-credential, require loyalty_code only for lookup, OR (b) add second factor for redemption (mobile-push confirmation, OTP to phone, PIN). Document phone-lookup as PII-disclosure risk.

findings.title: Mobile-app session token has full loyalty/redeem authority — no scoped ability
findings.finding: /api/loyalty/redeem is gated by auth:sanctum. Mobile-app sessions are typically Sanctum tokens without ability restrictions (vs. kiosk tokens which carry 'kiosk:order' ability). A leaked mobile session token gives full redeem authority on the user's own account. Combined with PLOY-2-R-04 (screenshot OCR of mobile-app QR), an attacker who steals a session can drain points.
findings.remediation: Add 'loyalty:redeem' ability on mobile-app session tokens. Require step-up auth (re-prompt password or biometric) before redemption > X€ — pattern available in Sanctum + custom middleware.

findings.title: Audit-log gap on cross-surface loyalty operations
findings.finding: Per CLAUDE.md §8 + §13 evidence rules, loyalty (money-equivalent) operations should write to audit_logs (chain-signed) for dispute resolution. Current pattern only writes to loyalty_transactions which has no HMAC chain. Disputes about 'who redeemed my points' have only Log::info lines (LoyaltyController line 320, AwardLoyaltyPointsOnDelivery line 144) which are not chain-protected.
findings.remediation: On every LoyaltyTransaction insert, also call app(\App\Services\Fiscal\AuditLogService::class)->write([action='loyalty.earn'|'loyalty.redeem'|'loyalty.refund', resource='user', resource_id=$userId, payload=[...]]). Owner gate due to volume impact on audit_logs.

findings.title: Kiosk-redeem trusts 'kiosk:order' ability for ANY customer's loyalty_code
findings.finding: Line 258: `$isKiosk = $caller && $caller->tokenCan('kiosk:order')`. Kiosk machine token can redeem on behalf of ANY customer who provides loyalty_code at the kiosk. This is by design (anonymous kiosk customer typing/scanning code) but the trust model assumes the customer is physically present. Same surface as PLOY-3-S-01 — leaked phone → kiosk impersonation.
findings.remediation: Document the trust model. No code change unless second-factor (PLOY-3-S-01 remediation) is implemented.

findings.title: GDPR opt-out path does not purge loyalty_transactions
findings.finding: Opt-out spec exists in mobile-e2e but no PHP controller method confirmed for 'delete my loyalty data'. loyalty_transactions has 6-year retention implicit (no GC). GDPR 'right to be forgotten' requires either anonymization (user_id NULL, loyalty_code NULL) or hard-delete. If hard-delete via users.delete cascades (FK ON DELETE CASCADE per migration line 32), ledger rows are deleted — possibly violating audit trail requirements.
findings.remediation: Owner+legal decision: which retention rule wins? Recommend anonymization (UPDATE loyalty_transactions SET user_id=NULL, loyalty_code=NULL, description='[anonymized]' WHERE user_id=X) on opt-out, preserving aggregate analytics without PII linkage.

blocker_for_v1: PLOY-3-S-01 is the worst — phone-lookup is a real attack surface. Recommend at minimum (a) disable phone lookup on /loyalty/check (require loyalty_code), (b) document the kiosk-trust-physical-presence model, in V1.0.2 add second-factor for redemption.
notes: Most concerns are systemic — single-credential design (loyalty_code) treated as money-equivalent. NF525 doesn't require this (loyalty is not fiscal). But customer-impact is real.
